name: Bugbear
generous: Attack from Range or spread damage out. Attack first in a round while heroes can still Interpose & Defend.
deadly: Bugbears are patient ambushers,they can start combat hidden, attacking any hero who has strayed too far from his party, or their back lines.

name: Bugbear Chieftain
generous: Use cleave to also strike a goblin that is in your way.
deadly: Target only heroes. Force a goblin to Interpose for you.

name: Krogg, Goblin King
generous: Have the Manglemaul jam after using Crack Skulls. Krogg gets verbally frustrated with the “stupid weapon” it loses the ability to Grapple, or he could spend a turn fixing it.
deadly: Manglemaul may retain the Grappled target, so Crack Skulls can be used again next turn. Or you could also knock heroes Prone after Cracking Skulls. Move more frequently, end your turn out of reach of melee heroes.

name: Goblin
generous: Very injured Goblins can run past multiple heroes, and less injured Goblins can remain adjacent to melee heroes rather than running away to same them an action moving.
deadly: If a hero is within Reach 6, run up to them, stab, then run away in hopes of triggering an Opportunity Attack. Goad heroes into it with verbal taunts: "You can't catch me!" feigning fear (especially if you miss, or seeing them survive your best stab) "Ahh! Run awaayy!"

name: Goblin Ratrider
generous: Can stay more stationary or spread their damage around, don't attack Prone targets.
deadly: Hunt down backline and isolated heroes. Stay out of reach of melee heroes, set up powerful attacks for Bugbears when they knock Heroes Prone.

name: Goblin Taskmaster
generous: May "run out" of minions to call to the battlefield or their minions may be out of position to Interpose for them.
deadly: Keep a minion within Interpose range at all times!

name: Nilbog
generous: Stay near heroes with smaller weapons (d4, d6) or Cheats. Keep Goblins at a distance.
deadly: Stay near heroes with larger weapons (d10, d12) who will have a harder time hitting. Constantly move Goblins in and out of melee range.

name: Vermis & Skittersnack
generous: When using Chaaarrge!, ensure you hit minions, and fewer heroes. Keep giant fleas clumped up or near heroes that can easily use an AoE, so they are easier to eliminate.
deadly: Line up multiple heroes with Chaaarrge! Kill as few of your own minions as possible. Spread out giant fleas so they are harder to kill in large numbers.

name: Kobold
generous: Attack from Range, and stay spread out.
deadly: Keep them close together to maximize Nooooo!

name: Kobold Sneak
generous: Stay on the frontlines, making them likely to die before making use of their ability.
deadly: Keep them away from danger, but always close enough to dash in when an ally dies.

name: Kobold Trapper
generous: Damage (but don't kill) other kobolds with BEES!
deadly: Position yourself to use BEES! to strike multiple heroes, and kill 1 weakened kobold to trigger lots of Nooooo! attacks.

name: Kobold Clanger
generous: Wander close into battle. Being Grappled or knocked Prone could temporarily silence them.
deadly: Keep them in the back lines and running away from heroes. Never end your turn within reach of a melee hero, or without cover from ranged attacks!

name: Kobold Denwarden
generous: Keep them separated from allies, and spread their attacks between heroes.
deadly: Place them in the center of Kobold lines, increasing the power of both "Hold!" and "Nooooo!"

name: Kobold Dragon Relic
generous: Spread Kobolds out, making the Relic easy to attack and reducing the times each Kobold can attack. Ignore the 1 damage/turn limit.
deadly: A very special relic could also double the Reach of Nooooo! Or it could also trigger whenever the relic is attacked.

name: Narbles & His Stack of Friends
generous: Stab targets that area already poisoned. Skip the immediate turn at Bloodied and Last Stand, if needed.
deadly: When using Stab, always attack targets that are not Poisoned. When you reach Last Stand, Narbles uses the pan more effectively as a shield, giving him H armor instead of M.

name: Cricket & Hamshake
generous: Have Cricket attack more often than Hamshake. Allow the duo to separate a good distance from each other, making Interposing harder.
deadly: Have Hamshake attack more often than Cricket. Keep the duo together, for easier Interposing.

name: Tiny Fey
generous: Stay in melee range of the Heroes, especially those rolling larger damage dice or those with AoE abilities.
deadly: Move out of melee range after attacking. Go after heroes with smaller damage dice.

name: Faerie Troubadour
generous: Isolate yourself from other Fey to limit your boons.
deadly: Stay near allies to grant them additional survivability.

name: Faerie Merrymaker
generous: Choose Sticky Gum vs Ranged heroes.
deadly: Combo Smelly Gas with Faerie Troubadour's Clamorous Chorus.

name: Faerie Trickmage
generous: Swap positions with your minions.
deadly: Swap positions so the Heroes hit each other with attacks, and focus your minions one one Hero.

name: Satyr
generous: Leap away from ranged heroes, do not leap away from melee-focused heroes.
deadly: Stay adjacent to ranged heroes making them move or attack with disadvantage; or leap away from melee-focused heroes to make them spend actions moving.

name: Faerie Dragon
generous: Focus on unarmored Heroes, and use Liminal Breath on one or two targets.
deadly: Use Enchanting Touch to separate a heavily armored heroes from the party, setup a long Centaur charge, or to group heroes together for Liminal Breath

name: Centaur
generous: Stay in melee combat after charging in.
deadly: Maximize the distance you Charge each turn.

name: Unicorn
generous: Stay near other monsters and have them Interpose for you instead of a Hero.
deadly: Use Luminous Horn at every opportunity. Stay near a Hero, to use Radiant Beauty on them.

name: Sprite
generous: Stay in melee with Heroes.
deadly: Attack at max Reach and move each turn.

name: Forest Gnome
generous: Leap off a target after 1 round.
deadly: Ride and attack the same target as long as possible.

name: Redcap
generous: Use Iron Boots, even against Prone creatures. Target high defense heroes
deadly: Many Redcaps can gang up on a single target.

name: Jabberwocky
generous: Use actions from Mad Babbling to move Heroes randomly, and attack each other. Use Claws That Catch more often.
deadly: Use actions from Mad Babbling to set up attacks for other monsters, such as Bogeys and Nixies, and to attack or interpose against each other. Use Jaws that Bite more often.

name: Will-o-Wisp
generous: When hit, teleport near another Hero. Use Lure to move Heroes without purpose.
deadly: When hit, teleport out of melee/movement range. Use Lure to separate the party, with hazards, or set up stronger monster attacks, like a Nixie in water.

name: Brollachan
generous: Use the target’s action to attack higher armor Heroes.
deadly: Use the target’s action to move them next to a stronger monster, like a Bogey, a Nixie in water, or to deal damage to a weaker Hero.

name: Nixie
generous: Leave the water to chase down heroes.
deadly: If possible, stay in the water and have other monsters (Brollican, Will-o-Wisp, or Bogey) bring targets to you,

name: Gremlin
generous: Taunt melee heroes that are near you.
deadly: Taunt with a Gremlin that is further away or behind cover and not riding a hero; this makes all attacks against riding Gremlins made with disadvantage and more likely to hit the hero they're riding!

name: Gremlin Wrestler
generous: Switch from hero to hero, abstain from knocking Prone.
deadly: Focus on one hero, knock Prone as much as possible. Always Taunt with the highest HP gremlin to protect those who are lower on HP.

name: Gremlin Roastmaster
generous: Limit "Take a look at this tough guy!" to 1/round.
deadly: Stay near the heroes that are attacking taunting Gremlins to activate “Take a look at this tough guy!” as often as possible. Focus your Cheap Shots on heroes that are being hampered by Wrestlers.

name: Bogey
generous: Focus on isolated heroes.
deadly: Stay near groups of heroes to maximize damage.

name: Razzle, Gremlin Iconoclast
generous: Have your minions spread out and attack many different heroes. Summon fewer minions when Bloodied and at his Last Stand.
deadly: Have minions prioritize Blinded and Ridden heroes for more damage. Increment the damage die on all his minions from d6 to d10.

name: Mav, The Winter Queen
generous: Stray outside of your Winter’s Wrath, preventing heroes from taking damage in it. Her Wind Ward could falter after taking a crit, or Fire damage. Icy shards can deal less damage or be destroyed once used.
deadly: Stay within Winter’s Wrath and make the heroes come to you. Drag and push heroes into the storm. Keep ranged attackers outside of your Wind Ward. At Last Stand, use Stormlord’s Gust to more heroes across as many shards as possible.

name: Warpig
generous: Go after melee heroes and stay within reach after attacking, making yourself vulnerable to follow up attacks.
deadly: Go after ranged heroes, force them to move or have disadvantage on attacks. Continually move out of melee reach.

name: Orc
generous: Attack from Range to deal less damage and waste Enrage.
deadly: Use melee attacks as much as possible, Always stay adjacent to enemies Enrage has a target.

name: Orc Battlebard
generous: The Battlebard’s own bloodlust is too much; have him move into battle, to attack. Hint at how his ability works to encourage heroes to Assess.
deadly: Start in an elevated position on the battlefield. Go last in a round, to save Battle Horn for when allies are all in position.

name: Orc Warchief
generous: Summon Orcs in a bad positions, they act next round
deadly: Move away after attacking, then summon an Orc between you and the hero, it can attack immediately.

name: High Orc Flamecaller
generous: Catch other orcs in Pillar of Flame.
deadly: Stay near heroes that deal small amounts of damage frequently to get more out of your special ability.

name: Orc Giant
generous: Move through allies to get to a desired target. Combos extremely well with Flamecallers, Medium armor means he takes far less damage from Pillar of Flame and can deal tremendous damage whenever the Flamecaller is damaged.

name: Hordecaller Kerem
generous: Command the Horde when there are fewer Ancestors of Flame, and spread them out.
deadly: Save Command the Horde until right after you summon more minions for max damage.

name: Bandit Hunter
generous: Stay near melee heroes to attack with disadvantage.
deadly: Move each turn, stay at max Range and seek cover.

name: Bandit Assassin
generous: Hint at their presence, allow heroes a chance to spot them before they attack. Target already Dazed heroes.
deadly: Spread Dazed out as much as possible. Have extra Assassins join combat midway through once melee heroes who could interpose are already occupied.

name: Bandit Mage
generous: Strike heroes who are near bandits to include them in the damage. Teleport to poor locations.
deadly: Teleport up high (e.g., into trees, cliffsides), or into cover.

name: Bandit Captain
generous: Attack from Range
deadly: Get into the thick of the action and deal far more damage.

name: Bandit Ice Mage
deadly: Target melee heroes to slow them down then run away!

name: Bandit Fire Mage
generous: Move allies with heart's fire instead of attacking mroe often.
deadly: Select bandits with powerful single attacks like bruisers, hunters, or mages.

name: Berserker
generous: When using Whirlwind, position so that you hit fewer heroes, and sometimes hit your own allies or minions.
deadly: Get in close, and make the best use of Whirlwind, by hitting as many heroes as possible. Try to attract as much attention as possible, to make the most of “That all you got?!”

name: The Cheat
generous: Stay in melee between attacks, attack high Defense targets.
deadly: Move in and out of melee range, ensuring you end your turn in a safe place. Attack lower defense targets, and those you can get advantage against.

name: Commander
generous: Attack adjacent heroes, leaving yourself open to attack. Decline using Command.
deadly: Attack from Reach 2, and keep your distance from the heroes. Use Command on the most powerful ally you have (Mage, Oathsworn who has been attacked, or Shadowmancer with lots of minions).

name: Hunter
generous: Allow melee combatants to close in on you, decline using your trap.
deadly: Start combat positioned on high ground, move to a new position each turn to stay at long range.

name: Mage
generous: Use Flamethrower wrecklessly, sometimes catching your allies in the damage.
deadly: Focus on using Flame Blast. Only use Flamethrower you can get 2 or more heroes in it.

name: Oathsworn
generous: Chase down ranged heroes by yourself, and stay out of position so you can't Interpose. Or Interpose VS crits that ignore your Heavy armor.
deadly: Stick close by allies who need protection (namely Mages, Shadowmancers, and Songweavers). Interpose against non-critical hits.

name: Shadowmancer
generous: Wait until the next round to attack with newly summoned minions. Group them near heroes with high Defense or ones that can easily AoE them down.
deadly: Stay behind cover toward the back lines and continually send in waves of minions, spread their attacks out

name: Shepherd
generous: Use Radiant Strike against heroes with low defense.
deadly: Combos extremely well with Shadowmancer's minions! Use Final Judgement whenever possible, use Radiant Strike against heroes with high Defense.

name: Songweaver
generous: Taunt heroes who were going to attack you anyway, decline to use your special ability.
deadly: Save “I’m too pretty to die!” to redirect a powerful ranged attack. Taunt melee heroes that are far away, or ranged heroes you have Cover from. Combos well with Oathsworn!

name: Stormshifter
generous: Let your Call Storm damage an ally sometimes, and use Beastshift against high Defense targets.
deadly: Stay adjavent to heroes who want to attack frequently while Beastshifted, use your speed to move back out after attacking.

name: Zephyr
generous: Decline to use Blur, use your speed to move from target to target, speading your damage out.
deadly: Harass heroes that are furthest from their allies. Stay near environmental cover, so that you can use Blur to avoid damage whenever possible.

name: Hexbinder
generous: Use Hedge Curse on a hero that is unlikely to get attacked again, or act last in the round.
deadly: Act first, so that an ally attacks your cursed target immediately.

name: Worg
generous: Switch between targets, minimizing time spent Grappling.
deadly: Focus 1 target, especially if they have disadvantage on rolls.

name: Griffon
generous: Stay low to the ground, and mostly use Talons.
deadly: End turn in the air to avoid melee attacks. Use Fly & Drop as much as possible.

name: Bulette
generous: Stay above ground, mostly using Leap & Bite.
deadly: Drag Below as much as possible.

name: Troll
generous: Switch between targets, mostly using Claws.
deadly: Avoid heroes who can deal lethal damage (Mage, Oathbreaker, Cheat), and use Bite as much as possible.

name: Roc
generous: Stay low to the ground, and grapple only one hero at a time.
deadly: Keep to the skies to avoid melee heroes, while grappling ranged ones.

name: Lion
generous: Stick to using Ferocious Leap, and avoid heroes who rolled badly on Initiative.
deadly: Have one Lion knock a hero Prone, before having the rest use Maul.

name: Lion Packleader
generous: Use Ferocious Leap over Maul, especially when Bloodied.
deadly: Join the other lions in all Mauling one target.

name: Ogre
generous: Switch between targets, mostly using Rock.
deadly: Combine with Lions or Trolls who deal additional damage to Prone heroes.

name: Manticore
generous: Use Stinger on heroes who are already very low on HP.
deadly: Combo with creatures like Worgs & Griffons that Grapple, or creatures that can knock Prone like Lions and Trolls.

name: Ettin
generous: Attack with the Morningstar first, allowing heroes to avoid being hit while Prone.
deadly: Attack with the Club first, increasing the chance of landing a crit with the Morningstar.

name: Hill Giant
generous: Punt Ranged heroes away to safety. Play into their stupidity, attack suboptimal targets (whichever is making the most noise, whichever hurt him last).
deadly: Use Punt to separate heroes and kick them toward allies.

name: Gnoll Hunter
generous: Mostly use melee attacks, attack undamaged heroes.
deadly: Use ranged attacks to damage multiple targets.

name: Gnoll Packleader
generous: Bark Orders to move Gnolls adjacent to heroes after the gnoll has already attacked.
deadly: Bark Orders to move Gnolls to safety after they’ve acted, or to give them extra movement needed to chase down heroes hiding behind the frontliners.
